response: A, your account says you felt afraid, wanted space, and did not agree to stay. Those statements match the shared facts that you asked to leave and could not. B, your account says you felt panicked and wanted to finish talking, and that you stood in the doorway because you believed a resolution was needed. Wanting to talk does not make blocking the only exit acceptable. A could not leave for five minutes after saying they wanted to go. Feelings on both sides can be real at the same time as that fact. If either of you feels unsafe, step away and seek outside support rather than forcing the conversation to continue.
